title: The walrus, hung
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The framed walrus goes on the shack's wall while Gully's out. The uncle points to the spot: beside the rules board, under rule four. Wood hangs it. Gully comes in, sees it, and says nothing for a whole panel. Then: 'That's under rule four.' The uncle: 'Rule four's about the counter.'

panels.composition: The shack. The UNCLE in the door in the chair, pointing. WOOD with the framed walrus and a nail. The rules board. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a young man holding a small framed drawing and a nail beside a board of painted rules in a bait shack while an old man in a lawn chair points from the doorway, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The walrus on the wall under the rules board. Rule four above it: NO DRAWING ON THE COUNTER.

image.prompt: close on a small framed napkin drawing hung beneath a painted board of rules, black and white, no words

panels.composition: GULLY in the door. Seeing it. A whole panel of nothing on his face.

image.prompt: a stocky teenager stopped in a doorway looking at a small framed drawing on the wall, his face blank, black and white, no words
a stocky teenager and an old man in a lawn chair, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Rule four's about the counter.' The walrus hangs there through 2027.
